summary.headline: Jyoti Resins Q2 FY27 volume grew ~15% and EBITDA margin recovered to 23% from 14.4% in Q1, with H2 margin guided at 24-25%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 sales growth of nearly 30% on roughly 15% volume growth, helped by price increases taken in Q1 after the VAM cost spike. EBITDA margin rose from 14.4% in Q1 to 23% in Q2, with gross margin around 63%. Brownfield capacity was raised from 2,000 to 3,500 tons per month and is now complete, with utilisation at 70-75%. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR 375-400 crore and FY28 to INR 450-500 crore, and deferred capital return decisions in favour of further market expansion.

financial_highlights.value: ~30% YoY (as stated by analyst, not disputed by management)
~150-160 days consolidated (per analyst's calculation; management cited 75-100 days for mature markets, 120-150 days for newer markets)
financial_highlights.change: Management aims to return to ~120 days

financial_highlights.value: INR 65 crore (analyst cited, up from INR 3.6 crore in March)

segments.name: Wood adhesives (Euro Adhesives brand)
segments.commentary: Core business; 14,000 dealers (up from 10,000 last year), 16 states after entering Odisha, with ~85% of revenue from five mature states and ~15% from newer markets. OEM share is ~6% of revenue, targeted at 10-15% over 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 375-400 crore, with 15-17% volume growth expected this year against a 20% annual target.
FY28 revenue expected at INR 450-500 crore; INR 500 crore is the stated first milestone, with INR 1,000 crore the longer-term ambition.
EBITDA margin expected at 24-25% in H2 FY27, subject to no sharp rise in raw material prices; management also cited a 22-25% band as its guided range.
Gross margin to be held at 63-64% in Q3, described as flat vs Q2.
Debtor days to be brought back toward ~120 days within one to three quarters; channel financing talks under way, with start expected in one to two quarters.
Greenfield facility in Gujarat planned at 1,500 tons per month for INR 45-50 crore; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Brownfield expansion completed in Q2 FY27: capacity raised from 2,000 to 3,500 tons per month (42,000 tons per year), at a cost of INR 6-7 crore; management says this can support INR 600-700 crore of revenue.
Capacity utilisation currently ~70-75%, providing headroom for existing and new markets.
Greenfield plant in Gujarat planned with 1,500 tons per month initial capacity and INR 45-50 crore investment; timeline not specified.
Plant to be open for investor visits from roughly the next month, per management.
Branches rose from 54 to 61 in the quarter; SKUs at 60-70 across 10 products.
demand_pricing: Price increases of ~6-7% taken in May 2026 by the company and the market leader; management says customers have accepted them.

VAM cost: pre-war ~INR 75-80/kg; spiked to ~INR 200 in Q1, fell to ~INR 100, then rose to ~INR 115 last month. Company says it held 90 days of inventory and contracts at ~INR 100, so the rise has not hit it yet.
Management says it has forward contracts for 60-90 days of VAM and has started direct imports.
Management said it would not cut prices or add discounts to defend margin; it is willing to accept 22-25% EBITDA to grow share.
October trading described as good; Diwali timing expected to help Gujarat and Rajasthan.
Industry category size cited at INR 7,500-8,000 crore; management says the company holds about INR 400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 sales reach the earlier ~INR 380 crore guidance, and is INR 500 crore achievable in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 at INR 375-400 crore and FY28 at INR 450-500 crore, with volume growth of 15-17% this year against a 20% target. It cited geopolitical and raw material risks as well as real estate slowdowns in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 24-25% H2 margin driven by gross margin or operating leverage, and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to raw material procurement ahead of the price spike, with marketing at ~7% of revenue in H1. It said a 65% gross margin and 22-25% EBITDA are achievable through premiumisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will trade receivable days come down, and will channel financing help?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is recruiting back-office staff and talking to channel financiers, expecting to start in one to two quarters. It aims to return to ~120 days, citing newer-market credit terms and a bad debt ratio below 0.5% over 20 years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong operating cash flow and can it continue to March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited internal accruals, debtor management and premiumisation. It said the brownfield capex is complete and marketing spend is the main use of cash, so it expects cash generation to continue to March.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company keeping cash on the balance sheet and not doing a buyback or dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is held because the sales team is being built out (650 people now vs 250 three years ago), and it wants to fund marketing and state expansion. It said it is too early to discuss buybacks or dividends, though one analyst argued for a buyback.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 growth came from weather, dealer meets and ground efforts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said weather and the low base from last year's rains helped. It credited around 3,500 carpenter meets in H1 vs 2,500 in all of last year, the Mirzapur tie-up, a CRM upgrade and new hires.

risks_watch: VAM price and crude volatility: management says a fall would be passed on as discounts if competition demands it, which could reduce margins.
Receivable days ~150-160 consolidated vs the ~120-day target; channel financing timing is uncertain.
Competitive pressure from brand leader and low-price regional brands; management confirmed it is keeping quality standards and not matching lower prices.
Execution of the 650-person sales team, the 14,000 dealer network and new-state expansion; channel repeat-order ratio target of 50% in year one and 75% in year two.
Q3/Q4 seasonality and the festive season; Q1 FY27 volume growth was only 9-10%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and the brownfield capex being complete, but more cautious on FY28 revenue and margins, which depend on raw material prices. Evasive on specifics such as the cash deployment timeline, receivable days and buyback, which management deferred.

adds.what: Brownfield expansion: 2,000 to 3,500 tons per month (42,000 tons/yr) at Jyoti Resins
Greenfield Gujarat plant, 1,500 tons per month initial capacity

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR 375-400 crore (about 31% midpoint growth) with 15-17% volume growth, backed by the completed brownfield expansion (now 3,500 tpm at 70-75% utilisation) and 14,000 dealers, though the Gujarat greenfield has no timeline and the growth plan lacks a concrete order book.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose from 14.4% in Q1 to 23% in Q2 and management guides 24-25% for H2 FY27, but this depends on VAM staying flat (now ~INR 115/kg vs ~INR 100 contracted) and the company says it is willing to accept 22-25% to grow share.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (brownfield done); Gujarat greenfield no timeline
rows.why: Brownfield raised capacity from 2,000 to 3,500 tpm (+75%) and is complete at INR 6-7 crore, but Gujarat greenfield (1,500 tpm, INR 45-50 crore) has no timeline, so new capacity in the window is only the brownfield already live.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume grew ~15% in Q2 vs 9-10% in Q1, management guides 15-17% volume growth for FY27 against a 20% target, backed by dealers rising from 10,000 to 14,000 and branches from 54 to 61.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 70-75% on the new 3,500 tpm base, so near-term need is limited, but the Gujarat greenfield is already planned and management deferred capital-return decisions in favour of market expansion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR 375-400 crore, with management citing geopolitical, raw material and real estate risks, and no sign of a raise beyond the existing range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management is more cautious on FY28 revenue (INR 450-500 crore) and margins, which depend on raw material prices; VAM rose to ~INR 115 last month and a fall would be passed on as discounts.

rows.label: Receivable days back to ~120 from ~150-160
rows.why: Management guides debtor days back to ~120 within one to three quarters, with channel financing expected to start in one to two quarters, but the analyst's consolidated estimate is 150-160 days and timing depends on the market.

rows.label: Entry into newer states (Odisha, 16 states) and OEM share 6% to 10-15%
rows.why: Newer markets are ~15% of revenue and the sales team has grown to 650 from 250 three years ago, with OEM share targeted at 10-15% over 2-3 years from ~6% today.

rows.label: FY28 revenue of INR 450-500 crore
rows.why: Management guides FY28 at INR 450-500 crore (about 20% above FY27 midpoint of INR 387.5 crore), but says it depends on raw material and market conditions and has cited real estate slowdown risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume momentum, dealer expansion and the completed brownfield capex, but cautious on FY28 revenue and margins tied to VAM prices; analysts pressed on receivable days (150-160 vs 120 target), the sources of margin, and why cash sits idle instead of being returned.
